newsitem.title: UK: Converting building societies to see cash outflow.
newsitem.headline: Converting building societies to see cash outflow.

text.p: Britain's Abbey National Plc said on Wednesday that up to two million savers would withdraw around 10.0 billion pounds ($15.9 billion) from accounts with building societies that are converting to bank status during 1997.

"This massive movement of money will start to flow as savers who have been locked in by the conversion process become increasingly aware of their freedom to shop around for the best home for their money," Abbey said in a statement.

The bank, which in 1989 became the first mutually owned building society to opt for flotation and bank status, said this was in addition to the 20-25 billion pounds expected to be paid out in share bonuses as five societies go public.
The Halifax, Alliance & Leicester, Northern Rock and Woolwich building societies have all announced plans to float, while the Bristol and West is to be bought by Bank of Ireland.
Building society members, the societies' savers and borrowers, are in line for pay-outs of in some cases several thousand pounds when their respective building societies float on the stock exchange.
Britain's largest building society Halifax is expected to be valued at around 12.0 billion pounds, Northern Rock 1.3 billion pounds and the Woolwich 3.0 billion pounds.

Abbey National said it believed that few of the customers of the societies involved, who will give up their membership of the savings and home lending groups when they float, "are aware of their freedom to withdraw from their accounts without losing their bonus entitlements".
These were, it added, subject to adhering to minimum conditions imposed by the societies.

It said that while most people believe they cannot move their money until after they have received shares, savers at the three largest converting societies "are already free to move the majority of their savings".
-- Alexander Smith, London newsroom +44 171 542 7719 ($ = 0.628 British Pounds)
